description: The reference answers for Fuaran.Compute.GeometricAlgebra over AUTHORED inputs (Phase 727, DECISIONS.md D85 and D86): the multivector of the conformal algebra Cl(4,1) and its products. A float is its IEEE-754 binary64 bit pattern as sixteen lowercase hex digits, or `nan`. A multivector is the list of its thirty-two coefficients in the order of `blades`; an operand written `{ basis: i }` is the basis blade of index `i`, `1` there and `+0` elsewhere, and `powersOfTwo` is the multivector whose coefficient at index `j` is `2^j`. `op` names the published function of the module `Multivector` and `input` its arguments; `expected` is a multivector, or one float for `coefficient`, `scalarProduct` and `squaredNorm`. Every cell is compared byte for byte, the sign of a zero included. A vector whose id begins `table-` multiplies one basis blade by `powersOfTwo`: each coefficient it answers is the signed sum of the `2^j` whose term reaches it, so the thirty-two vectors of a product spell out every term of its table and every sign. The products are one fold: each output starts at `+0`, the terms are visited ascending in the left index, then the right index, then the output, and each forms the rounded product of its two coefficients and then one rounded sum or difference, never a fused multiply-add, and never skipped because a coefficient is zero. `geometric-absorbed-then-cancelled` answers another scalar in another order of summation; `geometric-fma-witness` answers `-2^-60` where a multiply-add is fused; `geometric-every-scalar-term-a-negative-zero` answers `-0` where a fold is seeded from its first term; the `zero-against-infinity` vectors answer no NaN where a term with a zero coefficient is skipped. A negation flips the sign bit of a zero, a copy keeps it, and a grade projection writes `+0` outside its grade. Since Phase 728 (DECISIONS.md D87) an `op` written `Module.function` names a published function of the module `Blade`, `Point`, `PointPair`, `Line`, `Circle`, `Plane` or `Sphere`. A typed object is the list of the coefficients its type carries, in index order: a point the blades of indices 1 to 5, a point pair 6 to 15, a circle 16 to 25, a line 18, 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25, a sphere 26 to 30 and a plane 27 to 30; a Euclidean point, a direction or a normal is a list of three floats. `tau` is the threshold a zero test is given. An answer that can be refused is its own cell or `{ refused: <the case> }`, and one that has kinds is `{ kind: <the case> }` with what the case carries. Nothing is normalised unasked: an object built through points or by a meet has the weight its product gives. A quotient is one division, never a product with a reciprocal; a norm is `m × sqrt(sum((x_i / m)^2))` with `m` the largest magnitude; and at `tau = 0` the kind of a quotient is decided by the signs of its numerator and denominator, the quotient unformed.
